newsitem.title: CHILE: Aftershocks rock central Chile after earthquake.
newsitem.headline: Aftershocks rock central Chile after earthquake.

text.p: Aftershocks jolted central Chile after an earthquake on Sunday measuring 5.4 on the Richter scale, causing landslides and more damage to buildings but no injuries, officials said on Monday.
"There have been more than 40 aftershocks in the last 24 hours," Emilio Lorca, head of the Seismology Department at the Universidad de Chile, told Reuters.
"But the intensity has fallen sharply and we have only had one or two in the last four hours," he said.

Santiago was shaken on Sunday morning by an earthquake with an epicentre 25 miles (40 km) northeast of the tourist resort of La Serena which lies 300 miles (500 km) north of the Chilean capital. It lasted for 40 seconds.

One of the most intense aftershocks measuring five on the Richter scale rocked the area around La Serena early on Monday, causing panic among residents and cuts in power and telephone services, officials said.
Officials reported cracked walls and other damage to old adobe buildings in the nearby port of Coquimbo.
The aftershock also caused landslides on mountain roads near La Serena, Lorca said.

In Santiago, Monday's tremor registered just two on the Mercalli scale, which measures a quake's effects rather than its general strength. The tremors were barely felt in Chile's all-important copper mines which lie several hundred kilometres further north in the arid Atacama Desert.
